Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Samantha / Ben —

Quick operational summary from CS/ops:

- APAC sizing: for CarePoint’s stated profile (steady 200 req/s, burst to 600 req/s) we recommend a warm reserve of 2 x g5xlarge-equivalent nodes with autoscale threshold set to add up to +4 nodes on CPU/latency signals. Estimated reserved cost: $7,400/month. On-demand burst pricing estimated incremental: $3,100/month (based on expected bursts and token volume).

- Failover RTO: cold start of model caches to full warm state ~18–30 minutes depending on active KV size. With prefix/KV replication enabled and a short warm prefetch window (we can replicate last-3hr working set), expected re-warm time ~4–8 minutes and partial service in 90–120 seconds for low-latency reads.

- SLAs: We can offer 99.9% availability for EU primary with automatic weighted-traffic failover to APAC (failover policy in SOW). If you prefer a 99.5% SLA with lower committed capacity, we’ll reflect that in the quote.

- Compliance artifacts: attaching SOC2_TypeII_redwood_2026.pdf (on shared drive) and our standard DPA addendum link below.

Operational runbook excerpts (brief):
1) Pre-cutover: snapshot KV and config, validate dataset partitions, verify KMS key policy.
2) Cutover window: drain noncritical jobs, switch routing to EU nodes, validate canonical audit events.
3) APAC staging: enable replication; monitor latency and error budget for 72 hours.
4) Post-cutover: verify telemetry and schedule weekly validation for first 30 days.
